transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery and recovery. 

Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have some questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question! You should avoid any exercise for the first week after surgery. But after that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening.

Just make sure to avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month after your surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be able to keep using it as you normally would. If you're not sure, just check with your GP or care team to be certain.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, do let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Is there anything else you'd like to know about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's all for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they have. Thank you again!

verdict.label: fail

However, the agent did not convey `escalation_criteria` or `mild_case_advice`. The agent was interrupted after delivering only the first part of the canonical content for sensitivity to bright light.
